sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Docling converts documents such as PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, e-books, emails and audio into clean, structured output like Markdown, HTML or JSON for AI applications. It understands PDF layout, reading order, tables, code and formulas.
sixtySeconds.problem: Feeding documents to AI models is hard when PDFs scramble reading order, tables and formulas. Docling parses documents properly, can run fully locally for sensitive data, and plugs into LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI and Haystack.
whoFor: Data engineers converting large document collections
Agent builders who need document tools (MCP)
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for high-quality, local document parsing with a simple Python API and CLI. It started at IBM Research and is now hosted by the LF AI & Data Foundation.
requirements: macOS, Linux or Windows (x86_64 or arm64)

overview: Docling parses many formats, including PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, Apple Pages, Numbers and Keynote, OpenDocument files, emails, calendar files, audio and video (with speech recognition), and XML schemas such as USPTO patents and JATS articles.

Its PDF understanding covers page layout, reading order, table structure, code, formulas and image classification, with OCR for scanned files and support for visual language models like GraniteDocling. Everything is represented as a unified DoclingDocument and can be exported to Markdown, HTML, DocTags or lossless JSON.

You can use it from Python with DocumentConverter, from the docling CLI, as an API service (docling-serve) or as an MCP server for agents. It can run fully locally for sensitive or air-gapped environments. Individual models used have their own licenses.

tutorial.title: Convert a PDF to Markdown in Python
tutorial.useCase: Parse a research paper and print it as Markdown.

steps.title: Run this script
steps.code:
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

source = "https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.09869"
converter = DocumentConverter()
result = converter.convert(source)
print(result.document.export_to_markdown())

tutorial.expected: The Docling Technical Report printed as Markdown, starting with its title heading.
